newsitem.title: USA: FCC puts on ice NTT, KDD bids.
newsitem.headline: FCC puts on ice NTT, KDD bids.

text.p: U.S. regulators have put on hold their consideration of applications by Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp and Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd to offer international long-distance phone service.

The Federal Communications Commission, in letters to the two companies released Thursday, said the applications were being plucked from an expedited review process so the Clinton administration could review them for trade concerns.
The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative, the Commerce Department and the State Department said in a letter to the FCC that the applications "may raise trade policy concerns."

The departments asked the FCC to delay consideration of the applications while they are reviewed. The FCC, as a result, notified the two companies it is removing the applications from "streamlined processing."

In January, NTT said it planned to launch a special service later this year to provide Japanese multinational corporations with communications links between their offshoots in Europe, the United States and Asia.

Media reports in Japan have linked the delay in licence approval to Washington's irritation with Tokyo's insistence on keeping a 20 percent ceiling on foreign investment in NTT and KDD and to U.S. pressure to open up Japan's communications equipment market.
The following applications are affected by the delay:
-- KDD America Inc's bid to provide non-interconnected international private line resale services between the United States and Belgium, France and Hong Kong.
-- NTTA Communications Inc's application to provide facilities-based and resale services between the United States and all eligible international points except Japan.
-- KDD America's application to provide resale of public switched services to Belgium, France, Hong Kong, Mongolia and Russia. These are points where affiliates of KDD America are established.
-- KDD America's bid to offer resale of public switched services to all international points except Japan, Belgium, France, Hong Kong, Mongolia and Russia.
